title: AI Video Production Company: Hiring Checklist
summary: Choose an AI video production company by its workflow, product accuracy and rights checks. Require approved scripts, clear revisions and human review.
body_markdown:
## What should you test before signing a recurring plan?


Use a small, representative brief with written acceptance criteria. Our[AI commercial production guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ai-commercial-video-production) compares situations where filming, generation or a hybrid approach is appropriate.


Ask the candidate to explain what it cannot confidently reproduce. Review hands, product markings, apparent materials, object interactions, captions and voice synchronization. Check whether requested changes preserve the approved elements or require broad regeneration. Time the full review cycle, not just the render.


## What should a representative test project contain?


Use a project that exposes the supplier's normal work, including the part most likely to require judgment. A simple talking head may be a poor test if your recurring brief depends on precise product interactions. Conversely, an elaborate animation does not establish that the team can consistently produce clear, accurate presenter-led ads.


For an illustrative kitchen tool, ask for one short explanation using the actual product and one scene showing its operation. Supply approved product photographs and a recording of the real action. Ask the company to propose a treatment and identify which parts it can produce reliably. Make the acceptable product behavior explicit before the script is approved.


Request a brief response, a storyboard or scene outline, a rough cut and a final delivery. You do not need every internal generation attempt. You do need enough visibility to judge whether the company caught important problems itself and whether your feedback reached the final version.


Use an acceptance record with four outcomes: accepted, accepted with a minor correction, requires a revised approach or outside the agreed scope. Write the reason beside the outcome. This prevents an unresolved technical limitation from being disguised as a subjective disagreement about taste.


## How do you assess revision quality rather than revision count?


A revision allowance only helps when both teams understand what changes it covers. Ask how the supplier handles factual errors, execution changes within an approved concept and requests for a different concept. Review an ordinary example of each category using the company's own work or a permission-cleared sample.


Consider a fictional delivery in which the product label is wrong but the character, scene and script are approved. The request should be to correct the label while preserving the approved elements. Ask the producer to explain whether that is achievable with the current method. If the correction requires rebuilding the shot, record the implication before authorizing it.


A useful revision note has three parts: what is wrong, what the accepted version should show and which reference establishes that answer. “Match the blue cap in reference photo two” is more concrete than “the product feels off.” The client remains responsible for supplying a valid reference; the company remains responsible for executing the agreed correction.


After the revision, check the entire affected scene again. A correct label does not excuse a newly distorted hand or missing caption. This is a review procedure, not a claim that a particular tool always creates new errors. The purpose is to accept the delivered ad as a whole rather than approve isolated fixes without context.


## What should the final delivery package make easy?


Design the handover around the next person who must use the work. That may be an internal editor, a media buyer or the same supplier's campaign team. The package should make it clear which assets are approved, which are alternatives and which should not be launched.


Request an index containing the concept name, variant name, intended placement, destination, approval status and relevant rights notes. Add a human-readable description so the buyer does not need to open every video to find the version addressing a particular objection. Keep source-file and working-file requirements in the agreement rather than assuming they transfer automatically.


For a hypothetical three-concept batch, the folder could contain a demonstration concept, a routine concept and an objection-answer concept. Each can have approved variants with its own destination notes. Archive rejected cuts separately. Agree who updates the index when a product detail or offer changes.


Test the handover with one person who was not involved in editing. Ask them to identify the approved version for a given placement and offer. If they cannot, improve the naming and index before delivering a larger batch. A polished video library is less useful when the launch owner cannot identify the correct asset.


## How does the production company fit the wider advertising team?


Decide whether the supplier's responsibility ends with approved files or continues through campaign management. Knowlify offers end-to-end Meta ads with creative and campaign management together, alongside creative-only production for teams retaining their own buyer. The agreement defines the work, and Knowlify's plans start at $5,000 a month, with media spend separate.


For a creative-only arrangement, establish who translates campaign feedback into the next brief. Give the producer specific observations and the next question, not an unexplained request for more winners. For a combined engagement, ask how the same information moves between campaign decisions and production decisions inside the agency.


At the end of the pilot, evaluate product accuracy, usefulness of the creative reasoning, revision handling, delivery clarity and the effort required from your team. Keep those operational findings separate from campaign results. You can decide that a supplier is a good production partner while continuing to test which messages deserve more media investment.

## Key takeaways


- Evaluate the production workflow and finished deliverable.
- Approve difficult scenes before their variants.
- Keep permissions and speaker identity explicit.
- Use the[approval checklist](https://knowlify.com/articles/video-ad-approval-workflow) through delivery.


## FAQ


### Does an AI tool subscription replace a production company?


Only when your team can also handle the scripts, generation decisions, editing and review. Knowlify takes on those production stages and checks every ad before delivery, with Meta campaign management available in an end-to-end scope. Compare total cost and retained client hours; software access alone does not supply the people doing the work.


### Can an AI presenter say they used my product?


Do not invent a personal experience for a fictional presenter. Determine whether the script communicates a testimonial and have the underlying account, permissions and presentation reviewed before use.


### What does human review need to cover?


Ask for checks of product accuracy, claims, visual continuity, speech, captions, sound, placement composition and rights. Give each correction an approved reference and require a review of the complete revised version. The delivery record should identify the final approved file, intended use and the person who accepted it.


### Should I request exclusive rights?


Discuss the specific assets and uses with the supplier and an appropriate rights reviewer. Do not assume that permission to use a generated output automatically gives exclusive ownership of every element.
